## Claims
- [proved] For \(p,c\ge1\), hence in particular for \(\min(p,c)=1\),
\[
I_{j+c,i+p}\subseteq I_{j+1,i+1}.
\]
- [proved] The induced quotient map restricts surjectively as
\[
J_{p,c}\twoheadrightarrow J_{1,1},
\]
and induces a surjection
\[
Q_{p,c}=J_{p,c}/\Lambda_+J_{p,c}\twoheadrightarrow
J_{1,1}/\Lambda_+J_{1,1}=Q_{1,1}.
\]

## Strategy
Let \(B_{r,q}=\{\lambda:\lambda\subseteq q^r\}\). The Schur-basis box definition is
\[
I_{r,q}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\notin B_{r,q}}\mathbb Zs_\lambda.
\]
Since
\[
(i+1)^{j+1}\subseteq(i+p)^{j+c}
\qquad(p,c\ge1),
\]
one has \(B_{j+1,i+1}\subseteq B_{j+c,i+p}\). Taking complements gives
\[
\{\lambda:\lambda\not\subseteq(i+p)^{j+c}\}
 \subseteq
\{\lambda:\lambda\not\subseteq(i+1)^{j+1}\},
\]
which proves the ideal inclusion.

Thus there is a quotient map
\[
\pi:\Lambda/I_{j+c,i+p}\twoheadrightarrow\Lambda/I_{j+1,i+1}.
\]
Under the Schur-basis definition,
\[
J_{p,c}=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(i+p)^{j+c}}
\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda ,
\qquad
J_{1,1}=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(i+1)^{j+1}}
\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda .
\]
For a basis element of \(J_{p,c}\), \(\pi(\bar s_\lambda)\) is \(\bar s_\lambda\) if
\(\lambda\subseteq(i+1)^{j+1}\), and is \(0\) otherwise. Hence its image is exactly \(J_{1,1}\), proving the stated restriction is surjective.

Finally \(\pi\) is \(\Lambda\)-linear, so
\[
\pi(\Lambda_+J_{p,c})=\Lambda_+\pi(J_{p,c})
=\Lambda_+J_{1,1}.
\]
Therefore \(\pi|_{J_{p,c}}\) descends to the asserted surjection on \(Q\).

## Gaps
None, provided \(I_{r,q}\), \(J_{p,c}\), and \(Q_{p,c}\) have the stated Schur-basis and positive-degree-quotient definitions.
